boardDescription: A presentation built as a MeroDesign board: 8 screens, one of them tall.

data.content:
Apps that live on
your own nodes.

Private, collaborative software — with no central
server holding your data.
This deck is a MeroDesign board — itself a Calimero app.
Today, the cloud owns your data.

Your documents sit on
someone else's servers.

The provider decides who
can read them — and when.

Leaving means exporting —
if you're allowed to.
Sync is peer-to-peer. No server in the middle.
The app's state lives on each node
not in a data centre you don't control.
written in Rust, run by every node.
so concurrent edits merge with no coordinator.
only invited identities can read or write.

A team or organisation —
who you work with.

Who is in, and with
which capabilities.

One running instance —
this very board.

The WASM it runs,
published to a registry.
A namespace holds groups; a group's members share its contexts; each context runs one application.
Write the logic. Get the network.
typed client + hooks for the frontend
real nodes in CI, not mocks
Each one: your data on your nodes, shared only with who you invite.
A tall screen — scroll, or press Space.

The canvas calls update_element on your own node,
over JSON-RPC. Nothing leaves your machine yet.

The WASM checks your role, then writes the change
into CRDT state — a signed, mergeable delta.
The delta goes to your peers

Broadcast over the context's peer-to-peer topic,
encrypted for its members only.

CRDTs converge: the same result on every node,
whatever order the edits arrive in.

Each node streams the event to its frontend;
your teammate sees the shape move.

A node that was away syncs the missing deltas
when it reconnects. No server to wait for.

Your data. Your nodes.
Your apps.
